messages:
maria.dev: heads up — AcmeCorp pinged support: their Console streaming TTFT shows negative numbers (e.g. -124 ms) and tokens/sec oscillating between -200 and 0. They also saw a billing spike claiming ~50k tokens for a window where logs show ~2k. Customer is seeing intermittent 502s around the same time. Can someone triage? :eyes:

josh.support: thanks, can you paste org id + example request id and a screenshot of the dashboard window? also any recent deploys that touched the metrics pipeline?

maria.dev: org=acme-org-42, sample request id=req_2026_03_12_94 (redacted). Screenshot attached (console graph around 03:12UTC) — negative TTFTs are concentrated on the streaming tokens/sec rollup. No obvious deploy from the app team in last 24h.

maria.dev: repro snippet customer used:```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-2", "stream": true, "input":"hello"}' -i
```they said the API returned 502 then stream client retried, but metrics show negative deltas immediately after the first attempt.

monitor-bot: ALERT: streaming-ttft-rollup negative_delta detected
  org=acme-org-42 metric=ttft window=60s value=-124
  alert_id=sb-2026-03-12-007

kai-ops: @maria.dev thanks. negative deltas usually mean out-of-order timestamps or a consumer reprocess. Can you capture the raw events from the metrics topic for that window? run:```bash
kafka-console-consumer --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --topic metrics.streams --from-beginning --max-messages 100000 | jq 'select(.org=="acme-org-42")' > /tmp/acme-metrics.json```

maria.dev: grabbing that now. also, billing team: are there any recent changes to how streaming tokens are counted? it looks like tokens billed >> tokens emitted.

anna-prod: we rolled a change to the metric-rollup consumer yesterday (vistream-consumer v1.3.4) that alters timestamp rounding for variable windows. we did a quick smoke and didn't see negatives but will double-check.

liam-sre: @anna-prod that change could explain negative deltas if consumer writes an older timestamp after a newer one (out-of-order), rollups are naive and compute delta by subtracting previous cumulative. if the cumulative decreased you get negative TTFT/tokens/sec. pls check consumer commit af3c2b and the commit message.

josh.support: mitigation options for Acme: 1) temporarily route them to non-streaming endpoints (no rollup) 2) create a targeted alert to drop negative deltas from billing pipeline 3) issue a credit while we investigate. which does customer prefer?

maria.dev: Acme asked for quick mitigation — switch to non-streaming fallback and a credit. doing that now (will update ticket).

kai-ops: reproduced a suspicious pattern in the raw events: two events with same request_id but timestamps 03:12:05.300 (seq A) and 03:12:04.900 (seq B) — seq B landed after A due to consumer reprocess. payloads show cumulative_tokens went from 1987 -> 1835 (decrease). This produces negative per-window token deltas.

maria.dev: adding that to the support ticket. any quick fix besides rollback?

anna-prod: short-term: filter consumer writes where cumulative decreases (drop or clamp to previous) — I'll open a patch to clamp deltas >= 0 and backfill safe values. long-term: make rollup idempotent and use max(timestamp) per request_id.

liam-sre: agree. also we should check the billing pipeline upstream — if it consumes the same topic raw it might count both messages and double-bill. add a dedupe step by request_id + max_ts window.

josh.support: created support ticket #SUP-9283, applied non-streaming fallback for acme-org-42, issued provisional credit of $120. pinged billing and infra for follow-ups.

maria.dev: thanks everyone — I'll attach the raw /tmp/acme-metrics.json and the request logs to the ticket. please post PR numbers for the clamp and dedupe fixes so I can reference in the customer update. :thumbsup:

anna-prod: PR #512 on vistream-consumer: add-clamp-for-decreases. I'll follow up with PR #513 for dedupe in billing-consumer.

liam-sre: I'll schedule a postmortem once the fixes are in and we'll run a canary on a subset of orgs.

josh.support: closing loop with customer now. if anyone spots similar negative deltas in other orgs, ping this thread.

maria.dev: closing on our side — thanks team. :handshake:
